development_note: declared before any candidate run of these files, after the rustc oracle and baseline probes, and acknowledged by the integrator. rustc 1.98.0 gave every declared rustc outcome. The provider is spec/unsafe-negative-impls/provider.rs plus `impl !Error for &str {}`, core's same-head pair beside `impl<T: Error + ?Sized> Error for &T`. The baseline is main's C3 CLI (531b1f839, sha256 f35ec380): on this packet every client but the two orphan ones is rejected with `overlapping trait implementation headers require coherence proof`, unlocated, because the consumer re-proves the imported pair from its own perspective and cannot close `str: Error`; against the C3 packet, which has no pair, answer and answer-local-impl are accepted and the four local-ownership clients and the five opponents are rejected with that text located at their own pair. Both orphan clients are rejected on both packets with `library trait implementation requires a local type`, located at the client impl, before coherence
rule: approved design; no wire change. Coherence proves absence from the crate whose coherence it proves: a pair of two impls imported from one packet from that packet, any other pair (a client's own, a client impl against an imported one, and until a multi-packet profile one across two packets) from the consumer. Absence of a goal is knowable, as rustc 1.98's trait_ref_is_knowable decides it, when no downstream crate could implement it (closed inputs, or a concrete goal, as before) and that crate owns the trait, the trait is a closed language trait or a #[fundamental] trait, or that crate owns an input type (Self, then the trait arguments) after `&`, `&mut` and #[fundamental] nominals. rustc takes the first owned input with no uncovered parameter before it; closed inputs have none, so any owned input is that first one. Under a packet's perspective the consumer's own impls are never candidates: absence is decided over what that packet could see

observations: the provider exported under module-branches-v12 and module-nominals-v10 stops at `named, associated or generic alias transport requires its wider profile` on the baseline, as C3's provider does; the C3b rule is version-independent and changes no wire byte

the imported-pair failure on the baseline is unlocated (`input:`): an imported pair has no source key. C3b accepts honest pairs, but a dishonest pair in a forged packet would still be reported unlocated. Recorded as a diagnostic-quality item, not fixed in C3b
nonfundamental-wrapper uses the provider's existing plain `pub struct Slot<T> { pub value: T }`, which has no #[fundamental] attribute
limits: a pair across two imported packets is proved from the consumer, the conservative perspective, until a multi-packet profile records which packet is downstream; other packets' impls stay candidates under a packet perspective (presence only)
`dyn LocalTrait` and foreign types are never owned inputs; rustc treats a dyn of a local trait as local. Both are conservative

a packet cannot carry a #[fundamental] struct today (export stops at `general fundamental policy requires authenticated trait/nominal metadata transport`), so an imported nominal is never peeled; imported fundamental traits are the sizing traits, through their transported FUNDAMENTAL flag. Conservative
the input order is moot only because closed inputs have no uncovered parameter; a widening to open inputs must restore rustc's first-owned-input ordering
negative coherence over a `?Sized` negative impl's MetaSized premise stays Lane B's item; C3b does not change pay_negative
